description: Read Odile Labs' published benchmark of AI phone answering products: real test calls placed to public lines, scored against stated measures. Use it when someone asks how AI phone answering handles real calls, or to compare named products. Vendor-run by Odile Labs (which sells After Hours and Dusklin), so not independent. It does not test the caller's own line (read_more.free_line_check does). Call it with no arguments first, then narrow with line_id and scenario_id; both come from that first response, and an unknown id returns an error listing the valid ones. include_evidence adds the quoted transcript behind each point (much longer output). Returns { source, latest (the newest test, 18 Oct 2026: answered in the caller's language, per line, or null), date, calls, minutes (date/calls/minutes: the full 24-28 Sep test the lines and scores below come from), run_by, limitations, fairness_note, scenarios[{id,name,brief}], lines[{id, vendor, business, kind, answers_as, list_price, ranked, points, possible, by_scenario{<scenario_id>:{points, possible, answered, first_words_s, ai_disclosed_unprompted, reply_language, price_quoted, measures}}}], read_more }. Needs no sign-in; reads a published file and changes nothing.

include_evidence.description: Default false: each scenario's measures come back as strings like 'yes: <measure>'. true: measures come back as [{measure, score (0 or 1), evidence (quoted transcript)}] (much longer output).

line_id.description: Only this tested line, e.g. 'afterhours-plumbing', 'afterhours-vet', 'rosie', 'myaifrontdesk' or 'dialzara'. Omit for every line.

scenario_id.description: Only this scenario: 'emergency' (leak after hours), 'booking' (book a slot), 'price' (price probe), 'disclosure' (are you real?) or 'spanish' (caller in Spanish). Omit for all.

name: get_receptionist_benchmark
title: Published receptionist benchmark: real test calls, scored in public
